reviews.text: No excuse!. I struggle to read the Bible daily, even as much as I’ve tried to change my routine to incorporate daily scriptures! Since I found this app, I’ve been able to listen to all the scriptures and stories from a variety of pastors and leaders that help to spread the message of the Gospel! With this app, there’s no excuse not to be able to hear the scriptures! I listen when I can while I’m working, when I’m home doing laundry, in my car, while I get ready for work! Literally so easy! If I want to take notes I save the message I’m listening to so that I can refer back to it and apply these teachings to my life! No one said it would be easy to follow Christ, but it’s not called the Easy Life, it’s called a Better Life! I’m so thankful for the people that put this app together to reach that much further out to people! It’s 100% free, however it does give you the option to give to the ministries to help continue and further the mission of Christ.

With no cure in sight, PRAY is a safe harbor to receive His word and calming presence. 
Thank you, PRAY.

Love this app but… UPDATED!. I LOVE this app. I love that I get true Christian content that was meant to be shared straight from the Bible. The reason I give it three stars is because as a Christian we are to tell the truth and show love in that truth. As Christians we are to love people but hate the sin

I believe this also expands to who we support and who we let into our circle and what we stand for. I have heard ads that do not support Christian beliefs and I don’t think it’s right or Biblical to allow certain affiliations to sponsor this app. 

One that I think about in particular was an ad from Beauty Translated. Beauty Translated is a podcast created by a man who transitioned into a woman and talks about the experience of it and news about the trans community. Again, we are to love people but not their sin. Having an association with this type of background is not smart, not wise, and against everything Christians stand on and fight so hard for

I truly love this app but it’s making me question what beliefs are actually being portrayed and what message they are trying to share. Yes, it is mostly about The Word but you can’t have sin mixed in and think it’s okay

06/09/26 UPDATE to 4 stars: I have not seen or heard about that ad from Beauty Translated since my review. I have seen more Biblical based content and it has been amazing to see all the new things I now have access to

One bug I’ve noticed though is some of the picture art on the front of the sound tracks are generic ones that don’t explain what that sound track is. Not For Me. The app itself is polished and visually impressive, but the subscription system feels unnecessarily confusing. Signing up is seamless, but managing or canceling subscriptions is buried behind unclear menus and fragmented account systems. I ended up with both a monthly and yearly recurring charge and had a very difficult time even locating where to cancel them. For a spiritually focused app, the lack of transparency around subscriptions and billing management seriously undermined my trust in the platform.

Beyond that, the app felt far more focused on pushing an endless stream of featured audio content and personalities than actually helping cultivate a quiet, intentional prayer life. Every time I opened the app, something immediately started playing, and the overall experience felt more like a content streaming platform than a tool for reflection, prayer, or spiritual grounding.

I tried to bypass the free trial by hitting the “X” only to be directed to pay for a “limited time offer” of a week ad-free for $6. After patiently waiting the minute (typical ad length), I hit the faint“X” again only to be directed to another “limited time offer” to pay $6 per month instead of $14. This page also had a note of payment being so the creator could do whatever and no way to click off of it so I decided to delete the app. I was looking forward to trying a new app to grow closer to God but don’t like feeling forced into a subscription before even trying the product. My subscription ran out. I saw the ad free price tag and I thought “I’m not paying that I can read the Bible for free”. BUT…I’m hooked. I think there should be a warning that says “caution may be habit forming”. No seriously I did pause and thought about not paying. But it’s too good not to get. Part of what you pay goes to a ministry that you can choose. By going ad free…in a way you help the whole
Platform to succeed and in that way you are helping to spread God’s Word. Is the price kind of steep? Yeah. But let’s face it…we waste that much money on frivolous stuff. For a year of Pray.com ad free? Totally worth every penny. I can’t make it without Pray.com. 

One thing I’ve talked about before, one of the greatest little tools to keep you motivated, is the daily counter. If you show up for Pray daily it counts the days and if you miss a day it resets to one the next time you log in. It’s weird. You see that number go up and you just want to keep it going. Oh now I’ve missed plenty of days. I’ve been on Pray a long time and I’m only up to 187 days. But that’s the thing… it keeps you coming back. It motivates you when nothing else really does. Shouldn’t you be motivated enough by the Lord? Well yes but that’s not the point. The point is to keep you connected with the Lord. This is a minor feature . It seems insignificant but it is powerful. It keeps you coming back and coming back. I was reflecting on it this morning. Just thought I’d say something. Oh yes…GET THIS APP! It’s awesome.
Love all,
Coby
